item.title: Slow-burn Urgency
item.content:encoded:
Usually, I couldn't care less about any story directly linked to Armageddon, the Apocalypse, or any other type of religiously-flavored, end-of-the-world scenario. Not because the concept itself is inherently a bad one, nor because I detest anyone's religious beliefs— it's simply a concept that I've seen used over and over again, without any effort to actually make the event a unique, frightening experience for the reader. An outlandish statement, but I can think of several instances in various media where the "prophesied threat of world destruction" is downright laughable.

This proposal is a pleasant exception. While I was initially put off upon realizing "Oh great, it's an indestructible omnipotent thingy guarding an equally indestructible thingy that can destroy everything", I found myself slowly immersed in the Foundations shenanigans in response to it. The various experiments they conducted, the methods they resorted to, growing on a grander scale for each and every resulting failure, until suddenly, you're hit with the Apocalypse transmission that hasn't happened yet.

item.title: Nitpick
item.content:encoded:
The orders are telepathic. So there would be no way to know that most people were ordered to "FORGET". We'd just see them walking away with amnesia. The subject wouldn't remember the order, the researcher monitoring wouldn't have any reason to think an order even happened.

A minor hole in the plot, but it bugs me.

item.title: not_a_seagull's SCP Oddessy: Clef's Proposal
item.content:encoded:
Item #: SCP-001 (Clef's Proposal)

Author: DrClef

Review:

+ Review
- Review

Okay, so this is the most upvoted 001 proposal on the site, and for good reason, too. It links together several parts of the SCPiverse and just inspires so much awe. Let's go over it.

In case you're unfamiliar with Christian lore, this SCP-001 is the angel who guards the gate to the Garden of Eden. For those who don't know, after Eve ate the apple of sin, both Adam and Eve were kicked out of the Garden, and an angel with a fiery sword was left to prevent anybody from entering. The thing is, Clef never comes out and says it, he just implies it. Which is brilliant.

This not only ties together the lore of SCP-073 and SCP-076 (Cain and Abel, or the first two sons of Adam and Eve), it ties the SCPiverse to the real world, in a way. In addition, the ending implies that something terrible1 will happen in the future. And that's cool.

This skip isn't perfect, however. There isn't much narrative thread to hold it all together. But this was before narrative became a big thing, so I'll let it slide on that.

All in all, this skip has earned my +1. Great job, Clef.

Verdict: Upvote

Footnotes
1. In this author's humble opinion, it's the Rapture.

item.content:encoded:
This in my personal opinion.. does not fit what I would consider 001. What I take from it is this is essentially Uriel. Considering how Able and Cain were terrified to go to it whenever mentioned.

This in itself is an original idea, making one of the 7 archangels an antagonistic planet buster. However the numbers 001 have the ring of whatever that holds has an extreme sense of importance and transcendental/supreme being nature. However this is not what I would see as it, the thing is I could count 10 SCP's off the top of my head who are essentially more powerful than this SCP (such as 319). I wouldn't see a biblical spin off as the first of all SCPs. and the thing is the point that making it the first SCP discovered is not really that good of a spiel for my tastes.

I personally just prefer Swann's proposal as it doesn't have that "first SCP" but then gives the sort of supreme god taste. I would hate to just see it be numbered 3420 considering it is literally the prime cause and omnipotent of the entire series.
